articleTitle: PWM-modulation of GTO-converters with a cyclic resonant snubber: theoretical and experimental limitations
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A new class of voltage fed converters with resonant input link proposed recently by Divan are investigated when using GTO's as switches. After formulating the defining equations the peculiarities of applying GTO's as power switches are treated, with special consideration of storage time, switching losses and GTO turn-on restrictions. The limitations of pwm techniques, limitations to resonant frequency, electromagnetic inductor design and optimization are discussed. Experimental results for a prototype system are given.

articleTitle: Hibriede energie-topologie vir die verskaffing van elektriese energie aan gedesentraliseerde energieverbruikers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Electric energy at a moderate cost is one of the fundamental prerequisites for the development of any community. The supply of electric energy to decentralized communities is however associated with long, low power transmission lines, highly distorted supplies, high capital and maintenance costs and low reliability. Renewable energy sources are proposed to overcome the above mentioned limitations. Typical photovoltaic solar panels, small wind and hydro turbines and non-renewable diesel generators can be utilized as complementary energy sources, which can be combined in a cost effective manner with major savings on capital expenditure and thus with overall energy cost savings. This paper describes the topologies, cost analysis, computer-aided design and control of these hybrid energy systems.

articleTitle: Megahertz direct base drives for high power converters with high voltage bipolar power transistors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper examines the technology and miniaturization of direct base drives for bipolar power transistors up to 500 A. After considering various possibilities, it is shown that transformer coupled, carrier frequency systems are the only feasible solutions in this high power field. Different topologies are considered and a specific system using an internal frequency of 1 MHz is described. Experimental results and component details on the prototype are given.

articleTitle: Fifteen years’ data of lightning current measurements on a 60 m mast
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents 15 years of measured data of lightning strikes to a 60 m tall research mast situated in the Transvaal Highveld in South Africa. The peak amplitude, charge, and action integral, and rate of rise of current are analysed and compared to global data as analysed by other researchers. The paper concludes that there is no significant difference between the observations on the 60 m mast and data obtained from other areas of the world.

articleTitle: 1 000 kV Resistive divider for measuring non-standard lightning impulses
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the computer-aided design and evaluation of a 1 000 kV resistive impulse voltage divider intended for operation at an altitude of 1 425 m. Measurement errors are assessed at low voltage by comparison with a commercial high-voltage probe (ratio 1 000: 1, bandwidth 75 MHz). It is shown that the divider can acceptably measure non-standard full lightning impulses with front times as short as 0.5 μs and front-chopped impulses with chopping times down to 0.5 μs.

articleTitle: Electronic power conditioning: Some limitations, developments and applications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper reviews the present state of the art regarding power electronic switching devices, power electronic converter topologies, and the present theoretical concepts underlying the analysis and synthesis of power converters. Thoughts on the present limitations in power electronics are then presented, concentrating on the problems of conduction losses, switching losses and electromagnetic limitations. Developments regarding the use of non-linear turn-off snubbers, resonant techniques, driving technology for bipolars and other switches and selfoscillating converters with magnetic feedback are discussed. The contribution concludes by discussing some new applications that we have investigated, incorporating a number of the new developments that has been discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Generalised model of converters containing linear elements and switches which is suitable for simulation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: When modelling converter circuits one is faced with the problem of modelling the non-linear switches. A piecewise linear model of a switch is used to develop a generalised method to model most converter circuits in the time domain. This model uses a null current source and a null voltage source to model the on and the off modes of the switch respectively. This model allows one to formally derive the state equations, the output equations and the switching function of most converter circuits. Limitations of the method as well as improved models of the switches are discussed. A model of the auto sequential current inverter is developed to demonstrate the techniques used.

articleTitle: Space vector modulation — a real time application
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Space Vector Modulation (SVM) has become an attractive alternative method of pulse — width — modulation because of its relatively low harmonic production [1, 2, 3]. One such implementation of SVM [2] proposes a ROM based solution according to [1]. The operating conditions are calculated off-line and stored in look-up tables. These can be accessed at high speed, generating the control signals that drive an inverter to produce three-phase waveforms [2]. However, limitations on the ROM size imply a predetermined angular resolution, which causes distortions at, low modulation frequencies, and ficed proportions of such parameters as “minimum on-times” and “dead-band” imply that the PWM can not be tailored to suit a particular inverter implementation. This paper examines an alternative implementation of this PWM techfnique, which calculates the operating conditions and controls the inverter on-line, in real-time, using a high performance microprocessor.

articleTitle: A self oscillating bidirectional DC to DC converter employing minimum circuitry
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A fixed voltage dc to dc converter, featuring bidirectional power flow, is presented. It functions as a DC transformer, and to be cost effective the number of components in the circuit is reduced to an absolute minimum by making the circuit self oscillating. Kilowatt ratings at mains voltage levels are made possible by carefully optimising the circuit for effective base drive and snubbing of the transistors.

articleTitle: Protecting a gto under short circuit conditions
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: With the increasing application of the gate-turn-off thyristor (GTO), a need has arisen for improved self — protection under fault conditions where fast-acting semiconductor fuses are not available to fulfil this function. This paper covers the design of the driver — snubber — and protection circuits of a 25 amp 650 volt GTO used in a chopper circuit application. In particular it presents a method of protecting the GTO under both accidental overload and short circuit conditions. Practical results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: A new approach to analyse conduction losses in high frequency magnetic components
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A new modelling method for copper losses in magnetic circuits is presented. The analytically based two dimensional technique is capable of analysing and optimising the winding design all magnetic components used in present day power converters. A key feature is that the method, since it uses analytical equations, requires less computing power and can be implemented on smaller desk top computers. Predictions on the frequency dependent resistance of coils are compared to measured values and predictions by the classic equations of Butterworth.

articleTitle: Conduction loss minimisation in large bipolar power switches up to 500 a, in relation to base drive technology
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In large bipolar transistor power switches, conduction losses are critical as a design and decision parameter. Darlington power stages, compensated Darlington power stages and directly driven bipolar power stages are investigated, with the latter two analysed further as the lower loss possibilities. Losses as function of base drive current are investigated and shown to have a minimum value in both cases for very specific operating conditions. Control criteria for controlling both switches to operate at the minimum loss point are derived. It is shown that both have approximately the same dynamic characteristics, with the directly driven bipolar power stage being less complicated in this power range by a small margin.

articleTitle: Compensation of distortion current in power networks by power electronic converters
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper describes a first attempt at using reactively loaded, pwm converters as fast dynamic filters in a power network. The principles used are described, the current fed pwm converter used discussed and experimental results given as obtained on a variable speed drive as a non — linear load. The simulated and experimental results compare very well, and the technique appears promising for further investigation.

articleTitle: The classification of meteor trail reflections by a rule-based system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes a detailed new classification schema for meteor trail reflections. The schema allows fine distinction among identifiable subtypes within previous ‘large’ families, as well as the determination of ‘unknown’ types. Previous work done in the field is summarised with the importance of such a schema being highlighted. Some statistics showing the relevance of the classifications defined are presented and discussed. The design and implementation of the rule-based expert system used to obtain the classifications, together with its applicability and advantages in this environment, is discussed in some depth.

articleTitle: An expert system for the design of 3-phase squirrel cage induction motors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper deals with the use of an expert system in the comprehensive design process, in particular for the design of squirrel cage induction motors. A comprehensive design evaluation package had previously been developed and it was felt that the expert system could lead a novice in design to produce meaningful input data for the design of a machine of his choice. This paper describes the expert system and shows how easily induction motors can be successfully designed by being guided by the knowledge base included in the expert system. The value of such systems as a teaching aid is illustrated.

articleTitle: Understanding and designing a space vector pulse-width-modulator to control a three phase inverter
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Space Vector Modulation (SVM) is the name of a particular method of Pulse — Width — Modulation (PWM) for an inverter. This paper briefly explains the SVM algorithm and then describes its implementation using EPROMS to a transistorized three — phase inverter. Results are presented to illustrate the effects of gear ratio on the harmonic content of the inverter output current and these are compared with results predicted from off — line computer simulations.

articleTitle: On non-minimum phase behaviour in D.C. servo systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Interaction between the power circuit and the analog measurement and control circuits which can result in unsatisfactory, non — minimum phase behaviour is examined in low power direct current (d.c.) servo systems. Understanding the cause of this non — minimum phase behaviour allows the limitations resulting from it either to be avoided or to be included rigorously in the system design.

articleTitle: Unrestricted frequency changer using gate turn-off thyristors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The theory of the force-commutated cycloconverter in unrestricted frequency changer configuration is presented in a simplified form. This circuit converts a fixed-voltage fixed-frequency supply to a wide range variable frequency and voltage supply. Distortion is comparable to PWM inverters. The circuit needs no d.c. link and is capable of motoring and regeneration of A.C. motors.
